data.body:
Scope note on the private-slot-dir workaround: it is reachable only through the CLI, not through MCP.

Surfaced while an agent was running a plan review under a private `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` to avoid queueing on the shared four-slot semaphore. The workaround works from the CLI and does what it should. It cannot work through the MCP `review_plan` / `review_plan_start` tools, and the reason is structural rather than a bug in the fix: the MCP server is a SEPARATE PROCESS with its own environment, inherited from whatever launched it. An environment variable set in a client's shell — or by an agent about to make a tool call — never reaches that process, so the gate ops it runs resolve their slot directory from the server's environment, not the caller's.

Why this matters here rather than being a footnote. This ticket's remediation direction treats a private slot dir as the escape hatch when the host-global semaphore is contended. That escape hatch is available to exactly the callers least likely to be congesting the host — a local CLI invocation — and unavailable to the MCP surface, which AGENTS.md tells agents to PREFER for long gate ops (`review_plan_start` + poll, precisely because a gate can outlast the client's ~60s deadline). So the guidance steers agents toward the surface where the workaround does not apply.

Not proposing a fix here and not filing a separate bug — this is a property of the remediation's reach, so it belongs on this ticket. Two directions worth weighing when it is picked up: make the slot directory a per-request parameter rather than process-environment state, or have the MCP server resolve it from store/config so it is set where the server can see it. The second keeps it operator-controlled; the first makes it caller-controlled, which is what an agent actually wants mid-congestion.

Recorded from executed evidence, not inference: the CLI run under a private slot dir did proceed while the shared slots were held, which is what makes the asymmetry observable.

Reporting-quality note on this session, since it bears on how findings reach this ticket: the same agent also reported that the gate's suggested `rebar sign-review` remedy "would have papered over a refusal". I checked that against the code and REFUTED it — the message is conditioned on a PASS (`bugfix_size_gate.py:350`), and `resign.py:170-171` states and implements that it never signs a non-PASS/degraded/stale verdict. No bug was filed. Noting it so the refutation is on the record next to the accepted finding, rather than only the accepted half being durable.
